A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiMat work. Their complete 22 pages, including equations, Tables 1–4, Figures 1–10, and Appendix A, support reliable textual and visual comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original unconditional and conditional generation experiments, human preferences, and tree-search and error-repair analyses in Sections 6–7, with additional generated examples in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, human evaluations, analyses, and appendix examples.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects indices for rendering and discarding the new node, extending G_t to G_{t+1}, and feeding back I_{t+1}. These clarify the procedure already described in v2's Figure 2 caption and Section 4.2. The model, conditioning approaches, objective, search, and repair mechanisms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Substance 3D Assets collection for unconditional and inverse material generation, plus the same challenging filtered-material cases for human evaluation. Appendix A adds no different coverage between versions.

E2.justification: VLMaterial (SBS) remains the evaluated baseline against MultiMat's mixed and graph variants. Comparator membership is unchanged in the unconditional, conditional, parameter-optimized, human, and appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, model configurations, training settings, and metrics match. Both retain 100 unconditional outputs, 100 held-out conditional examples, and the human evaluation using 33 inputs, 40 candidates per model and image, and eight expert annotators.

E4.justification: The tree-search ablation in Section 7, error-repair analysis in Table 4, and qualitative comparisons and failure cases in Figures 6–9 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate and human-preference reporting. Neither reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–4, preferences in Figure 5, the Section 7 ablation finding, and qualitative outputs in Figures 6–9 match. For example, MultiMat (Graph)'s unconditional KID remains 2.365 and MultiMat+ (Graph)'s conditional DreamSim remains 40.367, using the tables' scores multiplied by 100.

T1.justification: The graph and intermediate-output definitions, cross-entropy objective in Equation 1, and backtracking rule in Section 4.2 are unchanged. Section 4.1's indexing corrections clarify procedural prose without revising formal assumptions, mathematical reasoning, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: multimodal graph feedback, incremental validation and tree search, and a full-feature CompactSBS transpiler. Claims about quality and efficiency relative to text-only baselines are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of graph conditioning, OCR-like errors, parameter optimization and KID, and error repair remain identical. The training-cost and data-availability limitations and Appendix A's failure-case discussion are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The CompactSBS documentation and complete Figure 10 example, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, image and token limits, hardware and training-time disclosures, and access information are unchanged. The corrected indices restate existing mechanics.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography match. No cited works are added or removed, and the positioning relative to prior program-synthesis and procedural-material approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.1's generation-loop paragraph receives localized wording and temporal-index corrections, particularly clarifying graph extension and updated feedback. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; terminology and document organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2's return-arrow label changes from G_{t+1}/I_{t+1} to G_{t+1}/I_t. Section 4.1's edits also cause minor page-4 text reflow. Tables and other figures, including all appendix displays, remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the central generation-loop description in Section 4.1 clearer by correctly identifying the new node, graph update, feedback state, and failed-node resampling. This provides a limited documentation improvement while the scientific evidence remains unchanged. The benefit is tempered by Figure 2's newly inconsistent I_t label, whose unchanged caption still specifies I_{t+1}.
